title: Opensubtitles keeps downloading same subtitles.
body:
Copying from another forum that told me to add it here.

I have every day if you look at my pictures. It is downloading the subtitles for ones I already have.  See picture. Every day it just grabs the same subtitles for things I already have subtitles for since you can see in my second picture every single one ends with .eng.#.  The number indicates that there is already a subtitle and so it just adds a .0 or .1.  Look at the third picture called Austin.  It is the EXACT SAME FILE that it has downloaded, 2 on the same day. Is there a specific setting I am missing that needs to be set so it doesn't keep downloading the same subtitles for ones already with a set of subtitles since it keeps downloading something I already have? It also doesn't even notice new movies and adds subtitles for them since it seems to think that it has no subtitles.

I forgot to add but for a long time there would be no subtitles added since I had added nothing. but May 25th (probably an update) it started adding in repeated downloaded subtitles.

Also do I just have a temp "downloading library" that I then send over to the main once I know they have all the subtitles?

comments.body:
I am also seeing the same issue. I think it's related to the fixing of issue [10696](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/issues/10696). That fix added a number to the end of the subtitle file. Prior to that it would just throw an exception in the log, which I think it why we never saw these duplicate files prior to that "fix". it seems like these two issues would be mutually exclusive. I don't want multiple same-language subtitles (same name, but add a number); however it seems that some users do.
Looking into it more, and pardon my lack of experience, but maybe there is a failure around the DownloadSubtitles method? 
It is supposed to check if an existing subtitle already exists and ignore, but it looks like it's passing the check?
 [SubtitleDownloader.cs](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/blob/master/MediaBrowser.Providers/MediaInfo/SubtitleDownloader.cs#L135)

comments.body:
which language is the one being downloaded? What does running this sql query on the jellyfin db return?
(I suggest not doing this if you don't know how to and/or haven't done it before as it is quite easy to mess up the db)

```sql
SELECT ms.Path, ms.Language FROM BaseItems b
JOIN MediaStreamInfos ms ON ms.itemId = b.Id
WHERE b.PresentationUniqueKey = 'YOUR_ID_HERE' AND ms.IsExternal = 1 AND ms.StreamType = 2;
```
Replace YOUR_ID_HERE with the id you see in the link when viewing the details page of that file
for example:
<redacted-host>/web/#/details?id=**80d909bd51d172d846f3f5be9de8ee8c**&serverId=irrelevant

Here's how I did it safely:

1. Go to your jellyfin config folder and find the jellyfin.db file. Mine is at `<config-root>/data/data/jellyfin.db`. There's also a jellyfin.db file in the folder above that for me, but that's an older version. 
2. Copy the db file to another location, like /tmp: `cp <config-root>/data/data/jellyfin.db /tmp/`
3. `cd /tmp/`
4. `sqlite3 jellyfin.db`
5. Use the above command to extract the data

It's not strictly necessary to copy it to another location because we're just `SELECT`ing, but for peace of mind this is how it can be done.
